question: Did the original Stage1 39-input families shift between training and the exact f696 evaluation path, and are predecision input-shift magnitudes different between weak and good windows matched by prior SOXX trend signs and first-trade year?

fixed_scope.input_order: Exactly the 39 original_features in the pinned source summary, no later minute-derived extra columns
fixed_scope.train: Qlib signal dates 2011-01-03 through 2022-12-30; use training finite median and standard deviation for each feature
fixed_scope.held: Exactly 944 f696 signal dates; retain partial 2023/2026 and complete 2024/2025
fixed_scope.feature_drift: Per held year and each original feature report finite coverage, held median minus training median divided by training standard deviation, and fraction outside training finite 1st/99th percentile; report all 39 without ranking or selection
fixed_scope.family_magnitude: Per day mean absolute (feature minus training median)/training standard deviation across finite family members; require all family members finite for a day
fixed_scope.window_outcome: Exact f696 rolling126 paired log excess below/above zero, diagnostic only
fixed_scope.window_start_state: Before first-trade 09:29, prior signal-day Qlib SOXX 5/20-session close-return signs
fixed_scope.matched_cell: Start state x first-trade year; compare only cells with both weak and good windows, weighting each cell by the smaller group count
fixed_scope.unmatched_2023: Preserve all 2023 windows and report separately; never infer a within-year contrast where no good window exists

interpretation: Feature drift and outcome-defined overlapping-window contrasts are descriptive reused-history evidence. They do not show causal importance, incremental predictive information, a tradable threshold, or SOXX strategy success. A separate frozen information and complete own-state 0bp account gate is required for any proposed factor change.
stop: Stop on source SHA/NAS receipt, Qlib calendar, feature order, training/held coverage, 944/819 account support, or signal-before-decision timing mismatch.
